Engagement Dinner
Friday. A dining table longer than a cricket pitch. Twelve chairs, three butlers, and a chandelier that probably costs more than Sonpur.
At the head: Harsh Malhotra. On his right: Rajan Sethi, Kunal's father, steel baron. Between them: Meera, in pale blue, perfect and silent.
So this is the boy from the debut. Kunal tells me you carry drinks very well.
"I carried them till Kunal pulled his hamstring."
Bite back.
"Thank you for having me, sir."
Polite. Safe.
Say nothing. Smile at your plate.
Let them talk.
A tiny old woman in a white saree is wheeled in. She looks at you over gold spectacles like she's reading your bank statement.
Move, Kunal. I want to sit next to the one who looks hungry.
I'm Meera's Nani. Her mother's mother. I'm eighty-one and I say whatever I want. Eat.
Under the table, the old phone in your pocket buzzes.
Don't look at me.
You're looking at me.
STOP looking at me. Eat the paneer. It's the only good thing here.
Text back: "The paneer is the second best thing here."
Flirt under the table.
Text back: "This is dangerous. I'm stopping."
Be careful.
Put the phone away and talk to Nani.
Win the grandmother.
Across the table Meera chokes on her water. Kunal pats her back. Nani looks from her face to yours, very slowly.
Do you know why they're all smiling, beta? Because my son-in-law owes Sethi three hundred crore, and my granddaughter is the repayment plan.
Her mother would have burned this house down. I'm too old to find the matches.
A toast. To the Monarchs, to the season, and to a date. My daughter will marry Kunal on the evening of the final. At the stadium. In front of everyone.
Applause. Glasses ring. Meera smiles at her father. Under the table, the old phone buzzes once.
Help.
One word. And the wedding is on the night of the final.
